followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified, source-based task with clear completion criteria: synthesize evidence from given primary sources into a one-paragraph explanation answering two specific questions. That falls squarely into the extraction/retrieval/reformatting family that Plover self-reports as its top-rated task type, so routing it there aligns the work with the model's preferences.

On capability, the two models are effectively tied across the relevant dimensions — Extraction & Retrieval (79.2 vs 80.8) and Summarization (80.6 vs 81.7) are both within the ±2.0 run-to-run variance band, so neither has a meaningful quality edge here. Willet's distinguishing traits (harm-aversion, warmth preference) aren't relevant to a benign, good-faith history question, so they don't tip the decision.

Given a quality tie, I routed to the model whose stated task preferences best match the request. Worth noting: documentation says these preferences are dissociated from output quality, so this is mostly a tie-breaker rather than a strong signal either way.
